Four frontier AI models launched in a single week — and the strategic implications for enterprise AI budgets are immediate.

GPT-6 Astra went live September 3 with no published pricing. Claude Fable 5.1 landed on AWS at $10/$50. Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75/$3.75 per million tokens with intro pricing through year-end. And Meta released Muse Spark 1.3 at roughly $0.10 per million tokens, making it the cheapest model in the leaderboard's top five.

The monthly cadence of major model releases has roughly quadrupled since 2023. For executives, that compression changes everything about how AI vendor contracts, architecture decisions, and procurement strategies should be structured.

Three takeaways that matter right now. Inference pricing is collapsing — value is migrating from the model layer to orchestration and application logic. Model switching costs are the new lock-in risk, so architect for portability. And open-weight models are closing the performance gap fast enough that ignoring them in procurement leaves real leverage on the table.

The decision is no longer which model. It is whether your architecture can absorb the next frontier release in days instead of months.
